programme.title: Wild About S1 - "Snakes"
programme.desc: With only a handful of snakes potentially dangerous to humans and most targeting rodents and pests, it seems their negative reputation today is unearned. Perhaps a product of their strange limb-less appearance, rather than their nature.

programme.title: Wild About S1 - "Raptors"
programme.desc: Many of the larger breeds of raptors are now endangered or vulnerable, particularly eagles, vultures and larger owls as they require large, specialized habitats. Though they may be soaring high now, the future doesn’t bode well for the great raptors.

programme.title: Wild About S1 - "Apes"
programme.desc: All great apes are highly endangered partly due to hunting and illegal pet trade, but mainly due to shrinking habitats. Sitting in the tree tops and jungles is a reminder of our past and our responsibilities for the future.

programme.title: Wild About S1 - "Spiders"
programme.desc: Commonly feared, spiders nevertheless persist in every part of the world in great numbers. Spiders are among the biggest groups of invertebrates with over 43,000 species.

programme.title: Wild About S1 - "Elephants"
programme.desc: Over a hundred people are killed every year by enraged elephants in India alone… with an additional 400 worldwide, though often seen as a symbol for calmness, patience and exotic nobility these true giants of the wild will need protection in the years to come.

programme.title: Wild About S1 - "Crocodilians"
programme.desc: Once highly endangered but now flourishing thanks to a concentrated effort to preserve their natural habitat, these ancient creatures continue to stalk waters as one of the last remaining predators on earth.

programme.title: Wild About S1 - "Wolves"
programme.desc: With populations steadily decreasing for decades prompting the forced reintroduction of wolves where the population has disappeared entirely, conservationists worldwide are struggling to keep the wolf alive and well.

programme.title: Wild About S1 - "Lizards"
programme.desc: Over hundreds of millions of years, they existed here long before us. Surviving natural disasters and mass extinctions, the are now among the oldest animals on earth.

programme.title: Wild About S1 - "Penguins"
programme.desc: Despite popularity, it seems the future does not bode well for the penguins, finding themselves in a shrinking world of melting snow and ice. However, they remain on the shores of our beaches and on the unforgiving Antarctic ice shelves and oceans.

programme.title: Wild About S1 - "Bears"
programme.desc: Bears today are divided into 8 species with some considered the largest land predators, though many are in fact omnivorous. They survive in our grasslands and mountains, tropical jungles and the cold harsh climate of the Artic.

programme.title: World’s Best Electric Cars
programme.desc: Alexis Conran investigates as the World gears up to make the switch from diesel and petrol to electric cars.

programme.title: Bright Now S1 - "Hacking our Microbiome"
programme.desc: Every person is playing host to at least 40 trillion non-human microorganisms. Collectively, these microbes constitute what's called our microbiome.

programme.title: Bright Now S1 - "School of Whales"
programme.desc: Follow a family of sperm whales in the heart of the Indian Ocean. Alongside a team of scientists, who have witnessed their most intimate moments over the past 7 years, we will lift the veil on the largest-toothed predator on earth.

programme.title: Bright Now S1 - "Message From Space?"
programme.desc: Deep in the mountains of West Virginia, the Green Bank Observatory has been receiving a mysterious signal from deep space. Could this be message from an advanced civilization, or is it a much stranger and violent occurrence?

programme.title: Bright Now S1 - "Coffee Buzz"
programme.desc: More than 400 million cups of coffee are consumed in the United States alone each day, making it one of the hottest drinks - even when served cold. Experts reveal some of the surprising secrets that make your favorite coffees taste the way they do.

programme.title: The Military Tech Show S1 - "NATO Maritime Centre, No Shipping-No Shopping"
programme.sub-title: NATO Maritime Centre, No Shipping-No Shopping
programme.desc: We visit NATO's Centre for Maritime Research and Experimentation in La Spezia, Italy. We learn how the world's oceans are one of the last places that military technology can be hidden from prying eyes.

programme.title: The Military Tech Show S1 - "Terrorist Threats, Sea Wasp Robot, Combat Medics"
programme.sub-title: Terrorist Threats, Sea Wasp Robot, Combat Medics
programme.desc: With an increasing terrorist threat to ports and shipping, the Swedish manufacturer SAAB has developed the Sea Wasp, an under-water robot for detecting explosive devices.

programme.title: The Military Tech Show S1 - "Warrior Vehicles, British Special Forces"
programme.desc: We're in Scotland for Unmanned Warrior, the key international military exercise using unmanned underwater, surface and airborne vehicles. We visit the Italian textile manufacturer who's kitting from a revolutionary new form of wool.

programme.title: Future Food S1 - "Episode 1"
programme.desc: In Lima, the capital of Peru which has been plagued by malnutrition, the future of food and farming is being reinvented as top chefs believe gastronomy can achieve social justice.

programme.title: Future Food S1 - "Episode 2"
programme.desc: Kanyan farmer and campaigner Moses Shaha is sceptical of biofuel. He journeys through southern Kenya, where farmers are starting to grow jatropha, to understand if the biofuel crop is a threat to farmland and food securuty as he fears.

programme.title: Future Food S1 - "Episode 3"
programme.desc: Exploring whether big agribusiness or small scale farmers are better placed to feed the world.

programme.title: Future Food S1 - "Episode 4"
programme.desc: In India, Tulika Verma is on a mission to ban junk food from Delhi's Schools, where one in six school children is overweight. India faces two possible futures: one healthy, and one a future of 'Western-style' diets and an epidemic of obesity.

programme.title: The New Frontier S1 - "From There To Here"
programme.desc: The first phase of this journey is complete, now commences the second, with robotics, advanced technologies and sheer daring we are now going where before we only dreamt.

programme.title: The New Frontier S1 - "Return To The Moon"
programme.desc: Few have walked on the moon's surface, though her allure remains strong, once again we are glancing her way with renewed interest and with a view to return very soon.

programme.title: The New Frontier S1 - "The Inner Worlds"
programme.desc: Venus the first and brightest star in the evening sky, and Mercury fleeting across the solar disk. As we begin to take a closer look at our companions they are posing more questions than answers.

programme.title: The New Frontier S1 - "Next Stop Mars"
programme.desc: It has fired our imaginations for millennia, Mars, the God of War and the source of Man's science fictional demise. It is the only other place in our solar system than Man might one day call home.

programme.title: Angry Planet S2 - "Hurricanes '07"
programme.desc: We hope Season Two will give us the opportunity to make the quintessential Angry Planet show – a full episode exploring a major hurricane that makes landfall in Florida or the Carolinas.

programme.title: Angry Planet S2 - "B.C. Caving"
programme.desc: In the porous limestone of Canada’s West Coast, great forces are at work under the ground, building and eroding the underground into fantastic shapes. In this episode we’ll witness George’s explorations of these massive underground cave systems.

programme.title: Angry Planet S2 - "Hot and Cold Crystals"
programme.desc: Miners in Chihauhau, Mexico, has just discovered an amazing sight. The Mexican authorities are only opening up the cavern to scientists and film crews – “Angry Planet” plans to be one of the first in!

programme.title: Angry Planet S2 - "Thunder Down Under"
programme.desc: In the first week of December – the height of storm season in Australia, we plan to travel with Jimmy Deguara, the most experienced of Australian stormchasers.

programme.title: Past, Present, Future S1 - "...of Comedy"
programme.desc: Comedy has always been a way for people to make sense of the world around them. As the world gets more complicated, how will comedy continue to evolve?

programme.title: Past, Present, Future S1 - "...of Hallucinogens"
programme.desc: While psychedelics were originally seen as a tool for spiritual enlightenment and healing, new research and studies are revisiting psychedelics to reveal their potential clinical and therapeutic impact.

programme.title: Past, Present, Future S1 - "...of Music"
programme.desc: We use music to nurture our children, comfort the sick, and worship the unseen. Music is inherently a human act, but today, artificial intelligence and algorithms have gotten more and more involved in music production, distribution, and marketing.

programme.title: Past, Present, Future S1 - "...of Communication"
programme.desc: From the first written word to the Internet, we’ve continued to innovate how we communicate with each other. What happens when technology advances to the point that ideas and thoughts can be shared instantly?

programme.title: The Curious Mind S1 - "What is Your Brain?"
programme.desc: We explore the apparently very simple question: What is your brain? This is something humans have been struggling to understand for millennia.

programme.title: The Curious Mind S1 - "The Social Brain"
programme.desc: The traditional narrative is that humans are selfish. If pushed the story goes we look after ourselves first and others later

programme.title: The Curious Mind S1 - "The Super-Charged Brain"
programme.desc: Our brain is always making decisions - Nigel explores how it does this and if we can help it to make better ones?

programme.title: The Curious Mind S1 - "The Imperfect Brain"
programme.desc: For most of human history our brains dealt with pretty straight forward problems. But that brain is the exact same one we now use to post pictures of our pets on social media.

programme.title: Combat Dealers S1 - "The Country Fair"
programme.desc: Military wheeler-dealer Bruce Crompton sees his local County Fare as a great opportunity to raisebusiness. Can he hunt down a German Schiwimmwagen to get noticed?

programme.title: Combat Dealers S1 - "The Russians Are Coming"
programme.desc: Bruce wants to impress a mega-rich customer - Russian Oligarch Slava - and offers him to drive his rare German Hetzer tank. Will Slava be lured into a deal?

programme.title: Combat Dealers S1 - "The D-Day Parachute Jump"
programme.desc: Bruce rises to a challenge to do a D-Day parachute jump. He hasn't jump in over 30 years but decided to do it in a genuine WWII paratrooper uniform.

programme.title: Combat Dealers S1 - "Bangs and Bombs"
programme.desc: Bruce Crompton takes money-man JHus on a picking trip to Germany. Hus gets worried when they discover a nuclear core from a secret Nazi nuclear testing factory.

programme.title: War Factories S1 - "German Aviation"
programme.desc: The untold secret story of war production that shaped the Second World War, beginning with how the German aviation industry came to dominate the skies of Europe.

programme.title: War Factories S1 - "Krupp"
programme.desc: The story behind the Krupp company, who were responsible for the manufacture of two of Germany's most feared war products - the Panzer Tank and the U-boat.
